headline: Rain-induced shortage: Vegetable prices surge in Dhaka
summary: Most vegetables now exceed 100 BDT per kg, while egg prices have risen by 20 BDT per dozen in a single week.
details: Heavy rainfall and supply shortages have driven up the prices of most vegetables in Dhaka's retail markets. Almost every variety, except for a few, now costs over 100 BDT per kg.
Egg prices have also climbed, increasing by 20 BDT per dozen within a week. Prices for various fish and chicken remain high.

Sellers attribute the price hike to flooded vegetable fields and transport disruptions caused by the rains, which have severely limited supply. Some traders are also accused of artificially inflating prices.
Hybrid cucumbers have jumped from 60-80 BDT to 120-160 BDT per kg, while local cucumbers now cost between 150-200 BDT. Egg prices rose from 120 BDT to 140 BDT per dozen.
Eggplant and bitter gourd have risen to 100-120 BDT per kg, and long beans are selling for 100-120 BDT. Green chilies have surged to 160-200 BDT per kg.
Conversely, papaya and tomatoes have seen price drops. Papaya is now 20 BDT per kg, and tomatoes have fallen to 150-180 BDT per kg due to increased imports.
Onion and potato prices remain unchanged at 40 BDT and 25 BDT per kg, respectively.
Retailers warn that these high prices are unlikely to decrease in the next 10 to 15 days until new supplies reach the market.
caption:
Vegetables in Dhaka are crossing the 100 BDT mark. Rain and floods have triggered a massive price hike.

Heavy rainfall and supply shortages have driven up the prices of most vegetables in Dhaka's retail markets. Almost every variety, except for a few, now costs over 100 BDT per kg.

Egg prices have also climbed, increasing by 20 BDT per dozen within a week. Prices for various fish and chicken remain high.

Sellers attribute the price hike to flooded vegetable fields and transport disruptions caused by the rains, which have severely limited supply. Some traders are also accused of artificially inflating prices.

Hybrid cucumbers have jumped from 60-80 BDT to 120-160 BDT per kg, while local cucumbers now cost between 150-200 BDT. Egg prices rose from 120 BDT to 140 BDT per dozen.

Eggplant and bitter gourd have risen to 100-120 BDT per kg, and long beans are selling for 100-120 BDT. Green chilies have surged to 160-200 BDT per kg.

Conversely, papaya and tomatoes have seen price drops. Papaya is now 20 BDT per kg, and tomatoes have fallen to 150-180 BDT per kg due to increased imports.

Onion and potato prices remain unchanged at 40 BDT and 25 BDT per kg, respectively.

Retailers warn that these high prices are unlikely to decrease in the next 10 to 15 days until new supplies reach the market.

headline_marked: US carries out [[air strikes on key Iranian sites]] for second night
headline: US carries out air strikes on key Iranian sites for second night
summary: Attacks targeting strategic cities and infrastructure have left several people dead and injured, according to local authorities and Al Jazeera.
details: The United States has continued its air strikes on critical Iranian installations for a second consecutive night. The attacks focused on the strategically important city of Sirik, known for its oversight of the Strait of Hormuz.

Similar strikes were reported in Bushehr, while two bridges near the port of Khamir were targeted. Local authorities reported that two people were killed and four others injured in these specific attacks.
In Bandar Abbas, strikes hit the Allahu Akbar area, including a residential neighborhood. Local reports state one person was killed and eight others were injured in that strike.
Additionally, railway infrastructure near Bandar Abbas was targeted, resulting in two more injuries. The US strikes also hit the Iranshahr airport, causing damage to the airport's infrastructure.
